content:
The image shows a banana fruit being held in hand. Here are the key visual observations:

**Affected part**: Banana fruit (peel/skin surface)

**Key visual features**:
- Yellow banana with extensive dark brown to black lesions
- Large coalescing irregular dark patches, concentrated heavily in the upper/middle portion of the fruit
- Smaller scattered satellite spots across the lower portion
- The stem/peduncle end also shows browning
- Lesions appear sunken, necrotic, and are spreading/merging together
- Background yellow skin is still visible in unaffected lower areas

**Differential reasoning**:
- **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum musae*): Classic post-harvest disease of banana fruit causing dark brown/black sunken lesions that coalesce into large necrotic patches — matches very well
- **Cigar_End_Rot**: Dry, ashy rot concentrated at the blossom *tip* end only — not a match (lesions here are spread across the whole fruit body)
- **Cordana_Leaf_Spot**, **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka**: Leaf diseases — not applicable to fruit
- **Bunchy_Top**: Systemic viral disease affecting whole plant/leaf morphology, not fruit surface lesions
- **Panama_Disease**: Vascular wilt disease causing internal browning of pseudostem/rhizome — not surface fruit lesions

The scattered-to-coalescing dark sunken lesions across the fruit surface on an otherwise yellow banana is the hallmark presentation of **Anthracnose**.
